title: Ewa Aganyin with Rehydrated Chillies
author: Lola Osinbajo
desc: A full cup of palm oil, onions browned ten to fifteen minutes, and the doneness cue nobody else gives — the pepper changing from bright red to dark red.
longDesc: This version sits between the other two: a full cup of palm oil, preheated until very hot but with no bleaching instruction, and a sauce built on dried chillies and dried red bell peppers rehydrated overnight or for two hours in hot water. Its real contribution is a usable colour cue. Where one source says very dark but not burnt and another says very dry but not burnt, this one tells you what to watch: the pepper changes from bright red to dark red. The beans take two to two and a half hours and are mashed to preference rather than to collapse.
steps: Pick the dirt from the beans, then rinse and drain several times.
Pour into a stockpot with the water and cook until very tender, 2 to 2 1/2 hours.
Mash with a potato masher or wooden spoon to the texture you prefer.
Rehydrate the dried chillies and peppers overnight, or in hot water for 2 hours.
Blend the rehydrated peppers with the onions, ginger and a quarter cup of water.
Preheat the palm oil until very hot.
Add the sliced onion and cook 10 to 15 minutes, until browned.
Stir in the blended peppers and cook 10 minutes.
Add the seasoning cubes, crayfish and salt, and cook 5 to 10 minutes more, until the pepper has changed from bright red to dark red.
chefTips: Bright red to dark red is the cue, and it is the most usable one any version gives. Watch the colour rather than the clock.
Ten to fifteen minutes browning the onions before anything else goes in. That is a long time and it is where the sweetness comes from.
Overnight is better than two hours for the dried peppers, if you can plan ahead.
Mash to preference here, not to collapse. This version keeps some bean texture where the Lagos street version does not.
Two to two and a half hours on the beans is longer than the other versions because the pot is larger and no salt management is specified.
A quarter cup of water in the blender and no more. You will be frying this and every extra drop has to go.
Nigerian honey beans — ewa oloyin — are named as the alternative to black-eyed peas, and they are sweeter and better suited to the dish.
commonMistakes: Blending the peppers with too much water.
Stopping while the pepper is still bright red.
Under-cooking the beans, which leaves them grainy.
Scaling the oil down so far that the sauce stews instead of frying.
sources: Adapted from 'How to make Ewa Agoyin (Ewa Aganyin) Beans an Stew recipe', byline Lola Osinkolu, cheflolaskitchen.com. Yield as printed: 5 People. Quantities as printed — beans: 1 lb Beans, 6-8 Cups Water, salt to taste. Sauce: 3/4 Cup Chili Dried, 2 Red Bell Pepper Dried, 1 Medium Onion, 1 teaspoon Ginger, 2 teaspoon Cray Fish, 2 Seasoning Cubes, salt to taste, 1 Cup Palm Oil.

Times as printed: beans 2 to 2 1/2 hours until very tender; rehydrate the peppers overnight or in hot water for 2 hours; onions 10 to 15 minutes until browned; blended peppers 10 minutes; final 5 to 10 minutes.

THE DONENESS CUE, verbatim and the reason this version is included: the pepper should have 'changed from bright red to dark red'. Compare 'very dark but definitely not burnt' (Sisi Jemimah, NGA031) and 'very dry but not burnt' (1Q Food Platter, NGA032) — this is the only one of the three that names a colour transition you can actually watch for.

Her headnote: 'This hearty ewa aganyin and it's sauce is perfect for those who truly enjoy flavorful spicy foods. Made with chilis (Cameroun peppers) and dried red bell peppers (tatashe) with lots of Onions!'
Note her gloss on tatashe as 'dried red bell peppers' — which puts her on the bell-pepper side of the tatashe dispute, against the two sources that identify it as poblano. See NGA019.
NOTE: no bleaching instruction appears on this page. The oil is preheated 'until very hot', which is a third position between bleaching for 10 to 12 minutes and explicitly not reaching smoking point.
Bean type: black-eyed peas, with Nigerian honey beans or Ewa Oloyin named as the alternative. Ginger is blended with the peppers if fresh, or added with the seasoning if powdered.
storage: 4 days refrigerated, 3 months frozen. Store the sauce separately.
reheating: Low heat, loosening the beans with a little water.
healthBenefits: Rehydrated dried chillies are concentrated in vitamin A precursors.
Cowpeas supply plant protein, folate and soluble fibre.
Red palm oil provides vitamin E and carotenoids.
culturalNote: Three named cooks, three ewa agoyin sauces, and three different positions on the single question of how hot the palm oil should get. Taken together they map the real range of the dish: bleached and almost black at one end, warmed and red at the other, and this one in the middle with the clearest instruction for telling when you have arrived.
